sentences.text: The decision rests on the Data Center claim. That segment supplied +102.5 percentage points of the company's +105.9% growth, and company growth sped up by 20.6 percentage points, so the revenue case is the whole case.

Customer concentration and supplier dependence are true but describe exposures the latest numbers do not show biting. The China export claim lacks its own test: China including Hong Kong revenue did not fall year over year.

The thesis is weakest on gross margin. The year-over-year test passes, but the sequential gain is +0.04 points, which the filing itself calls approximately flat, so the record shows a plateau, not expansion.

The record has no valuation or implied-growth analytic, so it cannot say whether +116.6% Data Center growth is already in the price. The step from 'growing' to 'stay overweight' is therefore unbacked here.
The CEO resigned after the newest 10-Q, with the CFO named interim CEO, and no filing in the record can show what that does to the next report.

A careful investor would next want to see whether receivable days, now 59.6 against 54.1, and inventory days, now 119.3 against 105.6, keep lengthening, because both say whether the growth is converting to cash.
The margin test has room of only 1.27x a typical move and held in 12 of 20 past readings, so one ordinary quarter could flip it.

Gross margin sits 0.2 percentage points below its level eight quarters ago, and the full fiscal year fell to 71.1% from 75.0%. The year-over-year gain is therefore a recovery to an old level, not a new high.
The filing ties the steep earlier rebound to the prior year's $4.5 billion H20 charge, a one-off that flatters the comparison rather than showing underlying expansion.
Revenue rose in each of the 8 quarters at a compound +15.7% a quarter, and Data Center is outgrowing the company. That makes the core premise broad-based in time, not one strong quarter.
Operating margin rose year over year with room of +5.4 points, and cost of revenue did not outgrow revenue. So far, the supplier and margin risks are not reaching profits.
Whatever China demand export controls removed has been more than replaced: China revenue did not fall, and company growth sped up.

On a fiscal-year basis, Data Center growth slowed by 74.2 percentage points, and the filing warns that faster product transitions may create revenue volatility. The quarterly acceleration is therefore not the only reading of the trend.

Receivables grew +126.8% against revenue's +105.9%, with a few direct customers each holding mid-teens shares of revenue. More of the reported growth rests on the payment timing of a handful of buyers.
Inventory grew +111.0% while cost of revenue grew +86.8%, and the last sharp margin drop came from an inventory and purchase-obligation charge. A flat margin leaves little cushion if that recurs.
Quarterly revenue stays above the latest $96.22B.
Gross margin stays above the year-ago 72.4% that the test uses.
Receivable days do not rise above 59.6.
Gross margin falls to or below 72.4%, breaking the margin test.
Inventory days rise above 119.3 while revenue falls below $96.22B.
An 8-K discloses a new export restriction or inventory charge like the H20 one.
Following the CEO's resignation, a later 8-K or the next results show a further senior departure or a change in guidance.
